records.translated_text:
My personal prop firm recommendations

For people without much spare capital → I recommend futures prop firms. (You can only trade Gold and Nasdaq-type indexes, though, lol.)

・Alphafuture
Its Trustpilot indicator is exceptionally high, so it's an excellent firm.
(I actually passed and withdrew $12000. After that, I misunderstood a rule and lost the account, lol → simply my own mistake.)
・Apex trading
It doesn't have Gold, so I'm less enthusiastic about it lately, but the price is low.
(I haven't used it myself, but one student on my plan passed five accounts, so it may be good.)

For people with some capital → a prop firm or an ordinary account

・FTMO
・5ers%
・Fintokei (yen accounts available)
・Fundra (yen accounts available)

If you want to trade in yen, maybe Fundra?
I haven't used it because it uses ctrader, lol.
Fintokei's Gold spread is wide, so it might be a little difficult to use.

But what all of these have in common is that it comes down to how well you can cut losses and make it a test of endurance. You need to change your approach somewhat from trading an ordinary account, so be careful.

Trading with Fintokei really does teach you the importance of risk management. If you don't understand precisely how the daily loss limit is calculated, you may carry an unrealized loss into the next day and see your loss grow by that amount. I didn't understand this rule at first either, so I learned the hard way, haha.
For example, when the daily loss basis changes, the reset time is UTC 0:00, which is 9:00 AM in Japan. By understanding rules like this and managing risk thoroughly, traders can trade more consistently. In that sense, I think trading with Fintokei is a good opportunity to learn how important risk management is.

📢 Weekly Prop Firm Report (third week of April 2026 onward)

This week was a period of quiet deepening for the prop firm scene, but negative voices and emerging risks stood out. Negative influencers and sellers of trading products continued to enter the space, and unexplained Blueberry Funded bans caused dissatisfaction on X and note. Meanwhile, Hantec Trader's major collaboration campaign became a positive talking point. Fintokei's simplified rules were consistently well received, giving Japanese traders somewhat more options.

🗣️ Main topics seen on X and the web this week (weighted toward impressions)
1. Negative influencers and trading-product sellers are increasingly prominent. The debate continues between claims that many prop critics sell products or EAs and criticize without showing proof of passing, and active traders demanding trading histories. Blueberry ban cases fuel claims that prop firms are dangerous and broker-backed firms cannot be trusted. Mixed with information from Manbou Sōsai, comments debate attracting newcomers versus avoiding dubious influencers.
2. Increase in unexplained Blueberry bans after the spring ban wave. Following March's rule easing, mainly around a 1.5% maximum risk, reports say accounts were banned for system violations despite following 1.5%, and that one account violation led to all accounts being frozen, a permanent ban, undisclosed reasons, and no refund. Sparse official explanations further erode trust. Trustpilot and elsewhere also mention selective enforcement.
3. Simplified Fintokei risk rules (VaR abolished, focus on the 3% rule). An update around April 15 clarified trade-group judgments and was praised as more intuitive. Traders using stop losses support it. Some call it a worsening, but longer-term traders view it favorably.
4. Major RZR Funded collaboration campaign. Starting April 15, a campaign offers a free Express challenge for depositing and trading with Hantec Markets. A $300 deposit and roughly three lots of trading can earn a free RZR Funded 1STEP challenge, potentially up to $200k. Hey Grok,
Fintokei is fun and good for learning to trade, but are there people actually making a proper profit?

Yes, there certainly are people making real profits. I completely understand the feeling that Fintokei is 'fun and good for learning to trade,' and that really is one of its greatest benefits. But there are definitely people earning serious money too.
How does Fintokei work?
In short, it's a prop firm (a funded trading firm).
You pay a challenge fee yourself (from several thousand to several tens of thousands of yen), take an evaluation on a demo account (steps 1 and 2), and if you pass, you can trade in earnest with virtual capital of several million to ¥50 million provided by Fintokei.
After passing, 80–100% of profits (up to 100% at the points stage) can be withdrawn as cash rewards (every 14 days, with an instant approval system).
In other words, it lets you earn with large capital while putting very little of your own funds at risk.
Actual earners and results (latest for 2026)
The clearest data is from the firm's annual 'Pro Trader Awards 2026.' 59
• Top tier: Little F — about ¥24.72 million in a year on a single account (nine rewards, 8,875% return).
• Other leading traders: several people at the ¥11.55 million and ¥11.44 million levels.
• Consistent earners: people who steadily get 18–20 rewards a year (for example, Yuki Haruna, third place in the Master of Payout award).
• Cumulative: total rewards to Japanese traders have exceeded ¥2.2 billion historically, with a payment record of about ¥2.2 billion in 2024 alone. 33
Recently on X (formerly Twitter), too:
• Reports such as 'I passed,' 'I've had 18 rewards,' and 'large withdrawals with a 10% monthly return' appear routinely.
• Interviews with award winners are published by coaches and communities, with 'steadily earning 1% a day' and 'risk management and consistency' cited as common traits. 47
In short, the survivors are those who **steadily build up 1%, not those who hit one flashy jackpot**. Fintokei itself says even 1% a week is world-class, so stable consistency is the strongest approach.
Cautions (honestly)
• The challenge pass rate is about 21% (roughly one in five).
• Only about 7–10% of all participants make it to a withdrawal after passing (repeated withdrawals are even rarer).
• The rules are strict (daily loss limit, total drawdown, minimum trading days, etc.), which is why it teaches you. Gambling-style trading leads to immediate disqualification.
So your feeling that it's 'fun and educational' is right on target; people who seriously develop their skills do earn rewards through this service. I think it is especially suitable for someone like you who trades FX (fx_gogogo).
If you're serious about trying, I recommend starting with a small plan (Quartz or Pearl) to get used to the rules. Those who actually earn all say it 'made them relearn risk management.'
Good luck!

Funded7 has updated its stop-loss (SL) rule.

This change does not mean "you may enter without an SL."

The basic principle is still to decide your SL before entering.

In actual trading, though, you may want to set the SL manually immediately after entering, a delay in operating the platform may cause the ATR standard to apply, or entering the SL may be burdensome in short-term trades.

So they added a buffer: if you place the initial SL within 30 seconds after entry, risk is calculated using the SL standard.

For beginners: the principle is to decide your SL first, but there's now a small allowance for forgetting to enter it or taking time to place it manually.

One caution: if the first SL is set at breakeven or somewhere more favorable than breakeven, the ATR standard may apply instead of the SL standard.

In other words, this is not a loophole. The change lets you reflect the intended stop-loss level within 30 seconds.

This is a useful improvement for short-term traders, but don't develop the habit of entering without planning an SL.

One step at a time: first, check the rules ☺️

*This is not investment advice.
*Confirm the final rules with the official announcement.

On Saturday morning, I was reviewing last week's trades while making coffee.

The trading results were better than I'd expected. My win rate was high, and I followed my rules when cutting losses, so I was satisfied with the outcome.

But for both winning and losing trades, it ultimately came down to whether I could act within my rules. In weeks with a good win rate, I waited properly for my entry conditions. In losing weeks, I was invariably looking at the chart too much and entering on a 'hunch.'

In the end, it wasn't about mindset or talent; it was simply whether I could follow the independent judgment provided by the rules. I got caught in this trap myself at first, haha.

Viewed as an extension of that, Fintokei's consistency rule is actually surprisingly fair, haha. It doesn't allow a reckless one-off win, but traders who consistently follow their rules can steadily build their balance.

Let's make next week one where we stick to our own rules.

Weekly trading report (May 18–May 22)

This isn't limited to this week, but I noticed something about The5%ers Bootcamp. As far as I can tell from my trading history, my swap points have never been positive, even though some trades are long high-interest-rate currencies and short low-interest-rate currencies.

I asked an AI about this, then contacted The5%ers via its dashboard chat and had the AI translate and analyze the response. Its analysis was as follows:

"In short, your question is entirely valid. The official response acknowledges that swaps in The5%ers evaluation accounts are 'deliberately distorted.'"

The key parts of the response, as translated and interpreted by the AI, were:
1. "swaps may not always mirror live market interbank rates exactly" — they do not match interbank rates and are different.
2. "swaps might appear predominantly negative" — they may mostly be negative.
3. "limitations or adjustments ... shown as negative consistently" — adjustments could cause a consistently negative display.
4. "not guaranteed to be fully symmetric" — long and short may not be symmetric; both could be negative.

From a trader's perspective, the AI interpreted that as: "Swaps on evaluation accounts are set arbitrarily, or intentionally unfavorably."

For position traders and traders who hold swing trades for longer, swap points may thus be unfavorable during a The5%ers evaluation challenge. That is how the The5%ers chat responded, so there is little I can do about it.

Even so, The5ers is highly rated as a prop firm. I suppose it has lasted so long because its strengths more than make up for such somewhat negative aspects. Prop-firm rules are constraints that challengers must accept. The path to passing has become longer, but I'll continue the challenge without blowing up the account.

Also, though I have not seen much about it on X, around 10:40 a.m. today BlueberryFunded forcibly closed positions carried over due to maintenance. Yesterday's email said this had been announced earlier in the week, but I couldn't find the email in my folder. I use Yahoo Mail, and if it went to the spam folder I wouldn't have seen it because I empty that folder every day. I am not entirely satisfied, but I can open positions again next week, so I'll move on.

Speaking of which, Fintokei is holding a contest and I have entered. Last time I traded as usual and was eliminated at the first hurdle. This time I'll raise the risk per trade and either clear the hurdle or destroy the account.

This week's assets: I closed the EURAUD positions carried over from last week, so Balance rose a little while Equity fell. There was no disastrous fall, and I'm glad I made it through another week without disqualification.

I've posted a lot about what I've noticed at prop firms this week, so I'll stop here. I'll keep trading carefully next week and beyond to avoid being disqualified or forced out.

For anyone who wants to try Flash Activation:
An explanation of the system and its terms

#ガチで出金まで行った人と繋がりたい

■ What is Flash Activation?
A system that's kind to people who paid a substantial amount at other prop firms only to be suddenly disqualified.

The Flash Activation Challenge has a particularly low initial fee. Once you pass the challenge stage, you pay an 'activation' fee to turn it into a Funded account!
Depending on the account size and conditions, the amount paid upfront is around ¥700–¥2,000.
*Payment is due upon passing, not upon payout.
*It varies with the conditions selected.
*As a guide, the activation fee for a ¥5 million account is ¥30,000–¥70,000.

■ What is a profit day?

A trading day that ends with a net gain. Please note that the criteria differ by plan.

• Flash Activation: A total of three days ending at least 0.5% up relative to account size are required.
• LITE 1-Step Phase 1: A total of three days ending at least 1% up relative to account size are required.
• LITE 1-Step Live: Only three trading days are required (no profit target).

■ What is the consistency rule?

It is a rule that one day's profit must not exceed 30% of total profit.

For example, if total profit is ¥100,000, the daily profit cap is ¥30,000. If you exceed this cap, you must accumulate more profit until your highest-profit day accounts for no more than 30%; you cannot withdraw until then.

The consistency rule applies to Flash Activation, but not to LITE 1-Step.

■ About stop losses

Not setting a stop loss is not a rule violation. However, trading without a stop involves considerable risk.

records.translated_text:
After trying several prop firms over the last few months—not only me, but many members of my private community too—one conclusion is becoming increasingly clear:

As is so often the case, cheap ends up expensive.

When you're managing small accounts of 10K, 25K, or even 50K, it makes sense to seek cheaper options and accept certain risks.

But once you start scaling to accounts of 50K or more, that changes completely.

At that point you're no longer looking only for the cheapest challenge.

You want the peace of mind of knowing that if you follow the rules, the company will honor its side.

For me, two names stand above the rest:

• FTMO
• FundedNext

FTMO still has something no other company has achieved: a reputation built over many years in the industry.

Years of paying out, and confidence in knowing exactly where you're trading.

FundedNext, meanwhile, continues to impress me especially with its speed. Support, verifications, responses, payouts—everything moves very quickly.

My two biggest disappointments have been:

Alpha Capital ❌

Extremely slow processes for practically everything, a very strict interpretation of the rules, and support that leaves much to be desired.

Funding Pips ❌

The main problem here has been spreads.

Too many times I've seen a trade stopped out by the spread when the price was near the stop loss, while that same aggressiveness mysteriously vanished when the price was near take profit.

I know spreads are part of the game, but when the pattern repeats over and over, it ultimately damages trust.

Does this mean there are no other interesting options? No.

But when we're talking about scaling serious capital, FTMO's and FundedNext's risk-reward proposition is hard to beat.

Saving a few dollars on an evaluation does little good if problems arise later when it's time to get paid and trade.

That said, it is becoming increasingly clear to me that profitable traders' natural path ends up being the same:

Eventually trading futures.

Prop firms are a fantastic tool for speeding up access to capital, but the more time passes, the more value I see in trading in centralized markets with clear rules and without depending on a private company's decisions.

I'll soon be taking that step myself.

I saw Fintokei's update, and it's hilarious how they immediately made sweeping changes for the Pro plan alone that are much worse.
With 2% and 3% DD, a 3% minimum payout amount is tough.

Here are my honest thoughts on this Fintokei update, lol.

In short, Slim is a good update, while Fast Pro and Swing are more selective and somewhat underwhelming.

■ Price increases for the top three plans

The new prices are:
• Sapphire: ¥109,800 (+¥1,000)
• Topaz: ¥209,800 (+¥10,000)
• Emerald: ¥309,800 (+¥10,000)

It's good that the most popular Sapphire went up only ¥1,000, but Topaz has crossed the ¥200,000 list-price threshold and Emerald the ¥300,000 threshold, so they now look quite a bit more expensive than before 🥲

■ Fast Pro plan update

▼ Main changes
⭕️ Plan prices reduced by 22–34%
✅ Added Iron with ¥1 million initial capital
✅ Profit target lowered from 10% to 6%
✅ Minimum trading days reduced from 5 to 3
❌ Reward rate lowered from 100% to 90%
❌ Maximum daily loss lowered from 3% to 2%
❌ Maximum overall loss lowered from 6% to 3%
❌ Evaluation step capped at 60 days
* Pro Trader accounts have no time limit
⚠️ Maximum daily profit is 3% of initial capital

▼ New plan prices
• (NEW) ¥1 million Iron: ¥9,800
• ¥2 million Bronze: ¥23,800 → ¥17,800
• ¥5 million Silver: ¥44,800 → ¥29,800
• ¥10 million Gold: ¥74,800 → ¥54,800
• ¥20 million Platinum: ¥119,800 → ¥93,800
• ¥35 million Diamond: ¥228,800 → ¥179,800

Fast Pro plan prices have become considerably cheaper!

But the hardest part by far is the maximum overall loss dropping from 6% to 3%.

The downside of halving the maximum loss is clearly greater than the benefit of lowering the profit target from 10% to 6%, lol.
(Honestly, it's still underwhelming even considering the price cuts.)

I'd recommend Gold to anyone who wants Fast Pro, but I think the Challenge Plan or Slim may be better‼️

■ Swing account update
* On a Swing account, the 5% maximum daily loss is calculated against initial capital rather than equity.

▼ Main changes
✅ All Challenge Plans except Emerald now support Swing
✅ Swap-free
❌ Approximately 1.2 times the price of a regular plan
❌ Maximum leverage changed to 25x

All instruments are swap-free, so neither positive nor negative swap is applied.

The question is whether the daily loss limit being based on initial capital and the swap-free feature are worth paying about 1.2 times the standard price.

It may suit a fairly narrow group, such as people who hold positions with negative swap for a long time.

■ Slim account update‼️

▼ Main changes
✅ Separate trading commission improved from ¥900 to ¥500 per lot
✅ BTCUSD and JP225 now also support low spreads
✅ Topaz now supports Slim accounts
❌ Plan price is about 1.2 times the regular version

I think the Slim account was the only good part of this update, lol.

It costs about 1.2 times more than the regular version (roughly the same as the early version), but the most important thing is to increase your chances of passing and requesting a reward, even slightly, so I think Slim is the best choice.

There's also now a refund system through the Fintokei Scaling Dojo, and I think the Sapphire plan is probably the best.

■ My conclusion
Slim → improved
Swing → worsened
Fast Pro → worsened

Taken on its own, the Slim account got a genuinely good update, lol.

This has become a long post, but that's all. Let me know what you think 🥺

The most quietly troublesome part of managing a Funded7 account was judging the position-size limit.

It's not a simple rule like 'up to 1 lot.' Instead, they use a statistical test:
• Calculate Q1, the median, and Q3 from the notional value of all positions.
• Compare the upper fence (Q3 + 1.5 × IQR) with 2.5 × median and use whichever is stricter.
• Anything above that counts as an 'outlier.'

Honestly, doing the calculations every time was exhausting.

If you want more detail, DM or comment. I'm not planning to distribute it for now.

records.translated_text:
On how to tackle The5ers Summer Plan 100K account:

I've decided to give up on aiming for four funded accounts.

There are several reasons.

I've secured $2,000 in the funded account, but after that all I can do is wait.

The payout cycle is two weeks, so I can generally secure 2% in about a week, but then I can't do anything until payout day.

The same applies to other CFDs, but I felt all that waiting time was very wasteful and inefficient.

With futures, by contrast, you can request a payout once you've achieved five profitable days, so you can make up to four payouts a month.

You don't have to wait in that way, making it far more time-efficient.

The5ers Summer Plan 100K has a $2,000 payout cap.
Lucid Trading 50K Flex has a $2,000 payout cap.

The plans look similar at first, but their different payout cycles make a big difference to the maximum amount payable per month.

Lucid Trading 50K Flex: up to $8,000 per month.
The5ers Summer Plan 100K account: up to $4,000 per month.
If payout efficiency matters, Lucid Trading 50K Flex has the advantage. That has made The5ers Summer Plan less appealing to me.

The 3% risk limit is also tough and my pass rate is poor. Copy trading is an option, but it takes time, so perhaps I'll just trade futures.

I lost in Fintokei's contest on day 3 because of one big mistake.
But now I'm glad I lost.
The reason is simple: even though it was a contest, I was able to trade with almost the same tension and state of mind as in live trading.
There was none of the complacency of doing it carelessly because it was a demo.

That is exactly why my weaknesses became completely clear: lax money management, missing checks before entry, no scenario, taking profits too early, cutting losses too late, and unstable emotions.

I felt down right after the loss, but experiencing my own issues under that pressure was significant.

Immediately afterward, I applied what I'd learned and traded on a live account, and I made a profit right away.

It feels as though losing in the contest and reflecting on it directly led to real profits.

This was my first trading contest, and I learned a great deal.

If you want a contest because you'd like to trade in a setting closer to real practice but still don't feel confident about live trading, I recommend it!!

records.translated_text:
It's strange, isn't it?

There are hundreds or thousands of affiliates around the world, yet only with prop firms do people say that if a prop firm has a problem, the affiliate is equally guilty.

If someone orders through Rakuten ROOM and gets sour oranges, I've never heard anyone say, “The affiliate is equally guilty, so the affiliate should pay half the cost!”

Maybe I just don't know, and people complain about other products too?

In the first place, if a buyer purchases an account at a prop firm they know nothing about simply because a famous person recommended it and assumes it must be safe, the buyer is at fault too (՞•̅㉦•̅՞)

After all, someone doing affiliate marketing is 90% on the company’s side (՞•̅㉦•̅՞)

When I do affiliate marketing, I make sure to ask the company, “May I write about the bad points in my article too?” and I do write about those bad points (՞•̅㉦•̅՞)

For The5ers, for example:
The spreads are narrow.
USDJPY is sometimes 0.
XAUUSD is relatively narrow too.
The commission is $4 per 1lot... I guess that's about average?
It's well known among prop firms and has relatively high credibility.

The bad points are:
Swap points are negative in both directions even for USDJPY.
There are reports and cases of payout refusal and payout delays.
Bulk trading is prohibited, so you can't repeatedly open positions in quick succession (՞•̅㉦•̅՞)
There is no yen-denominated account.

There may be other points, but if an affiliate doesn't write even one bad point, they just see listeners and fans as money (՞•̅㉦•̅՞)

The $25 entry price is a trap. For the trader. And for the affiliate.

If you pay for challenges or send traffic to prop firms, read to the end. The figures are sourced; this isn't a 'best prop of 2026' thread.

1) The calculation nobody puts in the hook

Official @Propr prices on Roya's challenges page (checked against Propr rulebook v1.0.5, July 27, 2026):

• Turbo 1-Step 5k = $25 → $23.75 after 5% cashback
• Turbo 1-Step 25k = $125 → $118.75
• Classic 1-Step 50k = $495 → $470.25
• Classic 1-Step 100k = $999 → $949.05

Price source: https://t.co/QOafuF1QvL
Rules source: https://t.co/3OokT5Mn8l (v1.0.5)

On a $25 5k account, you target 9% = $450. An 80% split = $360 if you manage a payout. One slightly oversized trade and the account is dead. You buy another ticket. Again.

On a $125 Turbo 25k ($118.75 net through my link): 9% = $2,250. An 80% split = $1,800 if you get paid. Same family of rules, no time limit, no consistency rule.

It's not 'five times harder.' It's five times more room for a fixed dollar risk. The $25 offer trains people to buy tickets again. The 25k forces you to have a plan.

2) What Propr is. Sourced. Without the brochure.

• On-chain prop, Hyperliquid perpetuals plus Polymarket prediction markets (https://t.co/oUS3SHEWZc)
• Flat 80% split across all sizes (rulebook, payouts section)
• On-chain USDC payouts on request, $20 minimum
• No time limit, minimum days, or consistency rule (rulebook and pricing docs)
• Bots/API permitted (Roya review and Propr docs)
• Funded accounts are simulated on the user's side; it's in their legal FAQ. You risk the fee, not a trading deposit.

Roya score: 86.7/100. A public scoring grid, not a bought badge.
Source: https://t.co/xkXFVoacWN + https://t.co/cfawm7YzSN

Payout I received: 153.91 USDC on August 22, 2026. A test, not a promise that you'll 'live off props.'

3) If you ALREADY pay FTMO/FundedNext/Apex

Don't habitually buy another challenge at full price.

Propr offers a 30% switching discount if you prove you're already a paying customer elsewhere (manual verification, code by email). It stacks with the 5% cashback calculated on the price PAID.

Classic 100k:
$999 list price
→ about $699 after 30% off
→ about $35 returned in USDC (5% of $699)
→ net about $664

Switch offer source: https://t.co/oXR0wiW0QP
The 30% comes from Propr. The 5% comes from my rebated commission. It's not a magic 35% discount.

4) The order. This determines whether you receive the 5%, and whether I get paid.

Propr attribution is fixed when the account is CREATED.

1. Create the account through the link
2. Take Turbo 25k (default), not the 'from $25' 5k
3. Funded → payout; see whether you scale
4. Fail → second try. Through Roya, I get 10% on the second attempt. Don't drop back to a $25 toy account

Without step 1: cashback is gone forever. Nobody can add it back.

Trader link:
https://t.co/cU7IkxseCA
(if the page isn't live: https://t.co/NTRdQbrqoo — same ROYA referral)

5) Who it is NOT worth it for

• Never paid for a challenge and just want to 'see' → okay, $25 once. Stop.
• You overtrade: changing logos won't change your drawdown
• US/UK: excluded by Propr (third-party reviews and docs)
• You want regulated CME trading or a name your bank recognizes: this isn't that product
• You're seeking the 'easiest' prop. Pass rates are low everywhere. Fee is nonrefundable

6) If you have an audience (X, YouTube, Telegram, site)

This part is for affiliates. Read it before DMing, 'Do you have a link?'

I'm not looking for 200 accounts putting a referral in their bio.

I'm looking for people who ALREADY speak to paying traders: FTMO reviews, funded trading, Hyperliquid, bots, comparisons.

What you get through me:

• Propr: 15% USDC on each challenge bought by your traders
• Moon (separate product, gamified trading, different landing page): 25% recurring — I take 10%
• Kit: landing pages, angles, payout proof, attribution order, net-price table
• Your Propr users do NOT get my 5% cashback (otherwise I earn zero on the override). They have your 15% reason plus the product. Don't mix the flows

What I don't do:

• Buy a score or a spot on Roya's grid
• Let you send self-referrals or multiple accounts
• Put Moon and Propr in the same post

If you do real 50k–100k volume, let's talk terms. The public 15% also exists directly with Propr. The reason to go through me: the kit, the explained switching-discount stack, follow-up, and Moon at 25% if it fits your audience.

DM 'affiliate' plus your platform plus one number (views or challenges already sent elsewhere). Not 'I want to make money.'

7) Why I publish the margins

On a $125 Turbo 25k, my direct rate is 25%; I return 5% to you if you came through MY link.
Eight 25k accounts give roughly the same P&L as forty $25 accounts.
Three 50k–100k accounts beat a week's noise of 'from $17.50.'

So I refuse to push the entry price as the main offer. $25 = giveaway/UI test. The 25k = an account.

records.translated_text:
I am reporting that the dispute with Funded7 over whether I passed has been resolved.

The conclusion is that I will be granted a Silver Funded account.

Thank you sincerely to everyone who shared and liked my posts. Without that support, I might not even have reached the negotiation stage.

At first, Funded7 ruled both Phase 1 and Phase 2 invalid. After several exchanges, the outcome is:

Phase 1 → valid
Phase 2 → valid
Retake → unnecessary
Silver Funded account → granted

The previous restrictions carry over:
Margin usage must always remain at or below 60%.
At most six simultaneous positions in the same instrument and direction.
Daily risk capped at 3%.

That is the settlement. I have also posted the emails and the course of negotiations for anyone interested. This closes the matter of Funded7's pass/fail decision. Thank you again to everyone who helped! 🙇

Negotiations with Funded7: timeline

① September 1–2 | Reached the Phase 1 profit target

I made nine genuine trades, mainly in GOLD, and reached the 8% (¥800,000) profit target. Funded7 also recognized the September 1–2 trades themselves as “genuine.”

② September 3 | Made a tenth trade of 0.01 lot

To meet the minimum of ten trades over three trading days, at 01:22 on September 3 I made a 0.01-lot trade, held it for two minutes, and lost ¥14. Funded7 later excluded it as an eligible trade, saying it involved no genuine market risk. Their count therefore became nine trades over two trading days.

③ Subsequently | Phase 1 passed → paid for Phase 2 → Phase 2 also passed

The system showed Phase 1 as passed. Trusting that decision, I paid the Phase 2 fee, proceeded and also passed Phase 2. This is the central issue in the negotiations.

④ September 7, 17:51 | Funded7's first review result

Funded7 suddenly reversed its decision. It said the 0.01-lot trade was ineligible, so the Phase 1 conditions had not been met. It invalidated the Phase 1 pass and the Phase 2 issued on that basis, offered a new Phase 1 free of charge, and required me to start everything again from Phase 1.

The initial position was therefore: Phase 1 pass ✕; Phase 2 pass ✕; funded account ✕; redo Phase 1 from 0%.

⑤ September 7, 18:53 | First formal objection

I protested: “If Phase 1 was a failure, why wasn't I told when it was marked passed? Why was I made to pay for and take Phase 2? On what basis was Phase 1 revoked after I had passed Phase 2? Shouldn't at least the Phase 2 fee be refunded?”

The issue here was that I had acted in reliance on the pass decision Funded7 itself issued.

⑥ September 7, 22:46 | Funded7's first concession

After the first negotiation, Funded7 changed its response. It apologized for the late notice of the review result and acknowledged imposing a burden on me through no fault of my own: I trusted the displayed Phase 1 pass, paid for Phase 2, completed it, and only then was notified.

It offered two choices:

Option 1: Take a new Phase 1 free of charge. Only Phase 1 must be passed again; the previously passed Phase 2 remains valid, no Phase 2 retake is required, and then I move to funded status.

Option 2: End the challenge and refund the Phase 2 fee, but not the Phase 1 fee.

The terms improved from “redo both Phase 1 and 2” to “redo only Phase 1.”

⑦ September 7, 23:42 | Second formal objection

I pressed further rather than end the negotiation: “Why must I start Phase 1 again from 0%?” The 8% profit had been legitimately achieved and Funded7 itself called the September 1–2 trades genuine. The only shortfall was the count of eligible trades and days after excluding the 0.01-lot trade.

I argued that I should be able to keep the 8% profit and add only the missing eligible trade and trading day. I also explicitly asked a crucial question: “Is this a violation of Rule 4 (improper use of the evaluation system)?” If it wasn't, why invalidate all of Phase 1 and the 8% profit?

⑧ September 8 | Provisionally selected Option 1

I replied that I chose Option 1, expressing willingness to pass only a new Phase 1, have Phase 2 waived, and then receive a funded account. After that, however, a further formal review result came from Funded7 headquarters.

⑨ September 8, 21:41 | Funded7 completely changed its decision

This settled the dispute. Funded7 stated explicitly that there was no Rule 4 violation. It formally confirmed that neither the September 1–2 Phase 1 profits nor the Phase 2 result were invalid. It then applied its own Rule 1, “Case A.”

Final decision: Phase 1 result valid; Phase 2 result valid; no Phase 1 retake; no Phase 2 retake; issue a Silver Funded account; move to Pro after three withdrawals on Silver. The substitute new Phase 1 account that had been issued was also withdrawn.

⑩ September 8, 23:07 | Accepted the final decision

I replied, “I accept the final decision. Please issue the Silver Funded account.” The negotiations ended.

In short: initially Phase 1 disqualified, Phase 2 invalid, redo everything from Phase 1 → after the first negotiation, redo only Phase 1 and keep the Phase 2 pass, or receive a refund of the Phase 2 fee → after the second negotiation, no Rule 4 violation, Phase 1 profit and Phase 2 both valid, no retake of either phase → final result: direct issue of a Silver Funded account, with a move to Pro after three withdrawals.

This is confusing too, so be careful.

Well, you've seen me talk about @ProprXYZ over the past few days and test its interface. I'll explain a little about how it works and why I like the project.

I'll say this up front: this time there will be an affiliate link, and I'll explain what I intend to do with it.

------------------------------------------------

1) Propr is a prop firm built around Hyperliquid. You buy a challenge and must hit a target without exceeding the loss limits. If you pass, you can access the funded account after identity verification.

Accounts range from 5k to 200k and can be paid for in crypto.

2) A 100k account does not mean they deposit 100k into your wallet, lol. You receive a share of the performance under their rules.

3) The Classic 1 Step rules are:

・10% profit target
・6% static maximum drawdown
・3% daily loss
・80% profit split on the funded account

On a 5k account, that's $500 to aim for and a $4700 floor you must not touch. Losses on open positions count too.

4) There is no time limit to pass the challenge, no minimum number of trading days, and no consistency rule. That gives you time to follow your plan without taking a trade just to fill a day.

But check the plan carefully: Turbo and the others have different rules.

5) What I particularly like is the interface. I've mentioned it before, but it's genuinely pleasant to use. You can see your positions, limits, SL and TP. It's well integrated and you know what you're doing. Well done.

6) Another good feature is that every payout can be verified on-chain. Payouts are made in USDC, and you can find the transactions on their transparency dashboard. You can see directly what was paid; anyone can check for themselves.

7) I've also spoken with the people running the project. They're very enthusiastic.

@louisregis regularly hosts live streams about progress and what they're building.

@velvetxbt handles business development well.

For me, being able to talk with the people behind it and follow the product's progress matters a lot.

8) An airdrop has also been mentioned around the project; I'll watch for confirmed details. I won't invent a date or tell you it will pay for the challenge. For now I'd rather focus on the product and how they develop it.

9) Currently there's 20% off all challenges until September 30 with code 2MPAID.

Check that the discount applies at payment and read the rules of the account you're buying; they aren't the same across all plans.

10) As for the affiliate link, you know this isn't my usual practice, but I decided to share my first link because I genuinely like and believe in the project. So I'll be clear about what has changed.

11) I get a 15% commission and promise to return the entire amount I receive from your purchase to you.

DM me if you use my link, and we'll arrange the refund once I've received the commission.

My link: https://t.co/yKtbWkrA9V
(If you don't want to use it because you dislike me, I don't care—don't use it, but at least try the product!)

12) It is still a challenge, guys. You can lose the fee, and a payout isn't guaranteed.

------------------------------------------------

Personally, what interests me is the framework for following my plan and, above all, my damn risk management.

Take the time to read the rules before paying for anything.

Cheers.

I passed Fintokei's Fast Pro plan 〰️‼️
I'm so happy 〰️
FTMO looks good.

[A slightly serious note]

Recently, I haven't been posting information about new prop firms on my sites. It isn't simply that I've stopped publishing information; the industry as a whole seems to be reaching a plateau.

First, there are hardly any new firms in today's prop firm market whose advantages are strong enough to surpass the established major firms.

Plenty of firms excel in one area, but is there any firm that can beat FTMO for forex, or Lucid or Topstep for futures, in overall strength?

Since 2024, many prop firms have closed or withdrawn. The survivors are increasingly concentrated among major firms with several years of operating history and a stable record of payouts.

In other words, the era when 'new is good' has passed. Isn't it becoming more rational to stick with firms that have a proven record?

I feel that LucidTrading is about the only newly launched prop firm that has surpassed the long-established firms. Lucid overturned the balance of power in futures prop trading within a year, which I think is truly impressive.

Conversely, in roughly the past three years, only about one firm has pulled off such a giant-killing upset. I think most cannot match the wide reach of the major firms.

As for the newer perps-related prop firms, this is how I currently see them:
Propr plans to enter prediction markets, so as long as I live in Japan, I don't plan to participate.
I might join Hypernova for now.
After checking Vest's rules and prices, I'd rather trade with my own capital.
Overall, I get the impression that maybe trading with my own money is enough, though I'm not entirely sure.

Also, introducing a new firm requires more than just reading the conditions on its official website. What matters most with prop firms isn't that 'the rules say payouts are possible,' but that a payout is actually made and reaches one's bank account.

In the past, some firms promoted their payment record right up until they closed, yet suddenly started denying payouts or collapsed. I know several of them myself.

Moreover, firm failures and rule changes have come one after another in recent years, and verifying the facts takes time.

Operating history, payout history, risk of rule changes, the trustworthiness of partner brokers, and licensing status all need checking. For an overseas firm, research alone can take weeks.

An especially important check is whether the terms allow rules to be changed retroactively.

The prop firm scene these days comes down to three things:
'Few new firms are trustworthy enough to recommend';
'Confirming actual receipt of payouts takes time'; and
'Industry turnover is too fast for safety checks to keep up.'
(The middle point partly reflects my own lack of ability.)

For forex, perhaps just use FTMO, and for futures, Topstep or Lucid. But what do I know?

records.translated_text:
I often read various people's forex sayings and find myself thinking, yes, that's true.
Come to think of it, how has my own thinking changed?
Compared with when I started, I think it's changed about 540 degrees 🙄

What am I consciously focusing on now...? Actually, there are probably lots of things, like not entering at certain points.
By repeating them, they become ingrained even without conscious thought.

I don't really lose anymore when I'm in a reasonably normal state, so I feel my attention is turning toward getting enough sleep, looking after my physical and mental condition, and noticing fatigue I might not be aware of 🤔

What scares me most is making strange trades when I'm not calm and blowing everything.
I never know when my inner “embarrassing commander” will emerge, so trading with prop firms puts me more at ease 👻

I'm still wrestling with five prop firms 💪
Among them, honestly, BlueberryFunded's detailed rules—especially the ban on reversing positions and the position-count limits—are a hassle, and I'm considering leaving 🤣

I copy trades from a small account funded with my own money into each prop account, so it's awkward when just one firm has its own unique rules 🤔

My entry EA can do things automatically. Well, I could design it around Blueberry's rules, though...

For example, I think many of you aim for the third wave, but I stagger entries during the second-wave correction, so position limits are troublesome 🙄
You don't know how far the correction will go, so you'd like to spread entries from the halfway retracement to near a full retracement.

I also aim for moves where a fake range breakout heads straight to the opposite side of the range. Those are attractive moves with a large risk-to-reward ratio, but a ban on reversing positions prevents me from doing that 🙄

By the way, I actually suspect the “wise commander” is the main personality in Oblivion Battery 🫠

records.translated_text:
Hello, friends.
I want to tell you what happened to me with @BlueberryFunded and ask for your support. On August 28, my $50,000 funded account was closed for allegedly breaching the daily drawdown rule. But that should have been impossible. Here are my calculations:

Trade 1: 0.16 lots from 3341 — maximum profit: $931, minimum profit: $691, difference: $240.

Trade 2: 0.46 lots from 3352 — maximum profit: $2173, minimum profit: $1481, difference: $692.

Trade 3: 0.2 lots from 3380 — maximum profit: $410, minimum profit: $290, difference: $120.

Total difference: $1052. So although my account had fallen by only 2%, my account and trades were closed as though it had fallen by 5%. They later said it was a mistake and returned the account. But their irresponsibility cost me three swing trades. Those trades would have brought me a $1600 payout and a second $50,000 account, whereas my account was at a 3% loss. This was an error that needed to be remedied, so I asked them to credit the balance my account would have reached if my positions had closed at my specified take-profit levels. But these irresponsible people brushed me off, saying the positions had already closed in profit and there was nothing to compensate. Yet for the trade I opened on August 21, I had set a take-profit level on August 27, five to six hours before my account was closed. In other words, I was acting according to a specific plan.

Today, I am experiencing the same irresponsibility again.

I had short positions in BTC, AVAX, BCH and XRP. Today my account and trades were closed again for the same reason: allegedly breaching the daily drawdown rule. But again there was no 5% decline. Here are my calculations:

BTC: 0.5 lots short from $113,640.5 — maximum profit: $2500, closing profit: $2136, difference: $364.
AVAX: 4 lots short from 30.82 — maximum profit: $1512, closing profit: $952, difference: $560.
BCH: 3 lots short from 546.3 — maximum profit: $429, closing profit: $28, difference: $400.
XRP: 3 lots short from 2.783 — maximum profit: $259, closing profit: $6, difference: $253.

Total difference: $1577, only 3%. The maximum daily drawdown level shown on my dashboard was $45,717. The balance at which my account was closed was $48,441.

I don't know what to call the repetition of such an amateurish error. Who else experienced this and lost their account without realizing it is another question.

We are fighting a psychological battle here more than a technical one, and these irresponsible people are affecting our trades. I don't want the same story to happen again. Whatever needs to be done, I want my account and trades restored. I would appreciate your support.

🫐BlueberryFunded rule change announcement 📢

The rules will change from May 20.

Changes:

✅ Removal of the margin rule

The requirement to maintain a margin level of at least 150% will be removed.

✅ Maximum lot sizes

A maximum lot size will apply to each currency pair.
*I've included an image.

✅ Martingale strategies

• Doubling the bet after a losing trade
• Increasing lot size by 50% or more after a loss
• Stacking large positions during a drawdown period

✅ Maximum number of positions

• Changed to a maximum of 4 positions on the same currency pair
• Added a maximum of 7 positions across all instruments

Those are the changes.

Personally, setting maximum lots instead of a margin rule saves me the calculation work, and the limit is plenty appropriate for gold, my main instrument, so I have no problem with it.

Overall, my impression is that the rules have become clearer rather than stricter.

However, I'm a little concerned that “stacking large positions during a drawdown period” is too vague.
Still, since it says “stacking,” I feel it might be fine as long as I don't average down, so I'll wait and see.

In any case, when using a prop firm, that firm's rules are absolute, so let's keep up with the information 👍

records.translated_text:
Recently I've become interested in something called prop firms, so I signed up for Blueberry Funded, which began offering its service in 2024 ☺️

Trading comes with restrictions, but to start, I bought an account with a $5,000 balance for around 5,700 yen. As I understand it, once you make at least 10% profit, you can withdraw 80% of the profit, normally on a 14-day cycle ☺️

The rules I understand are that losses, including unrealized losses and losses from stop-outs, of 4% or more in a day apparently disqualify you.
I think that's around $200, so it seems you fail if you fall below about $4,800 ☺️

You also fail if at least half your trades in a day are closed within one minute.

You fail if your margin level falls below 150%, too.
Averaging down or holding five or more positions also seems to mean failure for now, although I received an email saying averaging down would be allowed from the 20th.

I bought the feature that lets me withdraw once every seven days, so I reach the requirement at 20% profit, lol.
I think that means a balance of around $6,000.

If you keep the 14-day cycle, you can withdraw once you have about $500 or more in profit.

If you fail, the account disappears, and you then buy a new account ☺️

I don't know whether it's better than regular forex trading, but I think being able to trade large amounts with little starting capital is a good point ☺️
Metals such as gold apparently have 10x leverage, regular forex such as USDJPY has 30x, and cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin have 2x ☺️

I finished the first day up around $30 😅
I'm not used to low leverage, so I'm taking a wait-and-see approach for now.

I'm not really convinced, so I'll share this while venting a little.

For example, using 1–3 lots per trade on a 50-million-yen account.

It seems the few times early on when I played around thinking, “Yeah, I can effectively use 5 million freely with only 200,000 at risk,” have come back to haunt me 😂

Maybe it was a problem that I learned to adapt to Fintokei's rules, adjusted my lots appropriately—not too high or too low—and withdrew over 30 million 🙄🙄
Back then, they even asked to interview me as a success story...

Still, such sudden policy changes really make me worry about their finances.

My conclusion is that, overall, I still think it's a good prop firm.

records.translated_text:
There are a lot of voices defending Fintokei, so please let me speak from the perspective of someone who was banned 🙄

First of all, the basic point is that I paid the fees and traded within the rules FINTOKEI had set.

I was invited to the top floor of a hotel in Shinagawa and met the president and someone who seemed to be an interpreter and secretary. They told me, 'Even when you're a pro, it's still a demo with us.' They also said that meant I was free to trade.

They were the ones who provided accounts permitting high leverage and a daily loss limit of 5%.

So even if there were high-leverage traders, you'd expect them to assess the risk themselves and apply an appropriate ratio before using the trades on a live account, rather than connecting them directly. Normally that's what a demo account is for, isn't it?

Besides, this was my first experience with a prop firm, so of course I took the rules at face value 😥

With a maximum risk of 5%, if you find a good risk/reward opportunity, your read is right and your pyramiding works, you can make 10 million yen in profit. Once that account has such a cushion, you can ride the wave to 25 million yen in profit, which at 80% can mean a 20-million-yen withdrawal.

Even if that is inconvenient for them, it's the result of buying an account for the fee of two hundred and some tens of thousands of yen they quoted, within the terms they promised. If they dislike that, they should respond by raising the fee to a level with an expected profit for them.

If they think I'm going to fail, I don't think they need to single out pro accounts that already have profit limits and immediately force a ban on them.

In any case, abruptly overturning the promises they themselves set and unilaterally banning me with some plausible-sounding rationale can only be called underhanded.

On the last day, I did lose 4%. The account was still in profit, though.

That night, I received a warning about excessive losses.

So I contacted them: 'Wait, I'm trading within the written rules. What do you mean by excessive losses? If you put it in writing I'll follow it, so if there are secret rules, could you tell me? If my trading isn't what you want, I'll adjust it 🙇'

I received no reply to that message and was banned as things stood.

I really loved Fintokei. Actually, I still like it quite a lot.

Even the time I put the mysterious bath bomb the president gave me into the bath and it filled with petal-like things is a good memory 😭

But if you ask whether they acted honestly at the end, the answer is no.

So this is the one thing I want to say.

FINTOKEI did something underhanded in autumn 2024. That is a fact.

I want them to reflect on this and not do that to people who follow the rules in future, and to stop abruptly changing rules when things become inconvenient for them.

That's all. Sorry for the long post.

records.translated_text:
I've written my honest thoughts on the recent Fintokei controversy.
(I'm terrible at summarizing, so this is ridiculously long 🙇‍♂️)

[The fundamental premise]
This applies to money games such as domestic FX, offshore FX, prop firms, binary options and casinos: basically, firms' main source of profit is the money users lose.

Naturally, the real reasons behind warnings and account bans differ from the public explanations. Some offshore FX firms even give bonuses based on how much a client loses annually... lol.

Especially with prop firms and bonus-offering brokers, there will always be fraudulent users hedging across accounts, so payout refusal and ban rates cannot remain at 0% forever. (What happened until now was abnormal; as long as fraudulent users exist, a firm with a 0% ban rate will eventually fail.)

Honestly, given Fintokei's current revenue scale, I think even payouts from gambling-style trades are comfortably affordable. But I think they decided it wasn't wise to keep paying for fraudulent trades and gambling-style trading they don't recommend, which will likely keep growing, and took this opportunity to change direction in several ways.

(By the way, this is purely my gut feeling, so please don't take it at face value: I estimate Fintokei currently has monthly revenue of around 500 million yen and monthly payouts of around 200–300 million yen 🫠.)

Well, firms don't nitpick and refuse every large withdrawal indiscriminately; they want to keep operating as long as possible.

With Fintokei, educating traders isn't just a public pretext. They seriously aim to do it, within a scope that secures a certain amount of ongoing profit for themselves.

They presumably want skilled traders who manage risk to be introduced to partner firms and manage real money from scaling level 3 onward. (I don't know whether anyone can get there, though... lol.)

But ultimately it's a business. Large payouts earned through high-risk gambling-style trades that violate even part of a firm's terms, or trades suspected of being fraudulent, are more likely to be refused with a reason attached. To protect your payouts—your money—please keep the following in mind.

[What to watch out for at Fintokei from now on]
In conclusion, you need to avoid high-risk, high-return gambling-style trades and trades that could be suspected of hedging with other people or other accounts.

Given the profit structure, it's only natural: the larger the payout, the stricter the review; smaller ones tend to be overlooked.

During this controversy, a new standard was announced: 'Taking 0.5% to 1% risk per trade is a safe risk-management method.'

Combined with the current restriction criteria, I think anyone wanting to do everything possible to avoid restriction emails or bans would get no warnings with the following trading approach:

Leverage no higher than 25x; daily profit cap of 1% (40% of the profit target in evaluation phases); risk per trade of −1%; no economic-news trading; no account rolling; no substantially negative cumulative P/L in the pro trader account.

*The risk associated with leverage differs depending on holding time and instrument, so there should generally be one warning about excessive leverage first.

Trading is generally reviewed on promotion to pro trader and when withdrawing.

Those are very tight self-imposed limits to avoid being restricted, so I think occasionally exceeding them or proceeding at your own risk is fine. (I don't think Fintokei is quite that ruthless.)

Beyond that, I think it's an overall assessment of factors such as unnatural trading, number of trades, and how you passed Step 1 and Step 2.

[Penalties for gambling-style trading]
Fintokei's penalties for gambling-style trading generally have three steps: warning → restrictions → account ban.

However, warnings may be skipped if you've already received large payouts or if the trades are considered serious violations.

It appears that people banned on X this time were refunded for accounts still in the challenge and paid profits from pro trader accounts, but I think it will be case by case in future.

[To those restricted or banned this time]
On X, roughly 13 people in total have been restricted for gambling-style trading so far, and I think five of them were banned this time.

Previously there had been no ban cases even for violations. Honestly, I didn't think it was something to worry much about either, so I feel sorry for those who were trading seriously and suddenly got banned 😢

I think it looks different from the perspective of those involved.

It may be upsetting to hear people call Fintokei a good firm, or to have people around you treat you as gamblers.

Even if restrictions had been imposed before, I honestly don't think these sudden bans and the newly published risk-per-trade threshold were good. I think they were partly intended to make an example of people.

If you want to warn others against Fintokei as a bad firm, please do it to a degree that doesn't interfere with people who genuinely want to pursue trading seriously.

[In closing]
For traders who manage risk properly or want to, I think this controversy is positive because it extends Fintokei's lifespan.

I like the rush of gambling-style trading too, but high-leverage traders will always eventually blow up, whether they make 10 million or 100 million yen along the way. If Fintokei hadn't appeared, I think I would eventually have gone bankrupt at Exness, so I'm grateful.

Still, more restrictions aren't welcome, are they?

If you can't trade under these restrictions, I think you can go to another firm or return to offshore FX. Even now, though, I personally think Fintokei is superior overall.

To everyone continuing to trade with Fintokei, let's do our best 💪 (Sorry this got long 🫛.)

records.translated_text:
I only learned about prop firms very recently, but the more I look into them, the more attractive I think the environment is for traders—enough to wonder why I didn't know about them before.

At a prop firm, you trade on a demo account provided by the firm rather than using your own funds, and receive rewards based on your performance.

You can focus on trading without taking on the risk of losing your capital, and the clear risk-limit rules are designed to help the basics of money management sink in naturally.

Of course, an exam fee is required. But being unable to pass also means that, if you traded real money, you would probably lose it rather than grow it.

I think the prop-firm environment, with its clear pass-or-fail criteria, is especially well suited to people who relax too much on a demo, fail to stick to money management or can't take it seriously.

I tried Fintokei because I wanted to use my own EAs.

In actual operation, however, my EA portfolio's style of riding trends to build large profits often did not mesh with prop firms' particular daily loss and profit caps.

Even when I wanted to let profits run, reaching the cap triggered a forced stop, making it difficult to use the EAs' inherent strengths.

So partway through I switched to mainly discretionary trading. I've now passed Fintokei's first exam and am taking the second.

I also develop EAs and trade FX through a corporation, so if I pass Fintokei's exams, I'm considering trying Fundora next, since it allows corporate trading.

records.translated_text:
Take it from someone who threw away around 1.6 million yen at Fintokei: prop challenges are nearly impossible for beginners.
Passing on the first try is extremely unlikely.
If you're dreaming about it, I think you're better off not doing it.

For reference, I've attempted the Sapphire 20-million-yen plan 16 times, lol.
(100,000 yen each, times 16!)
If someone like me says it, you can count on it!
If you aren't confident in your skills, seriously, don't do it 😭

To be fair, I passed through Step 2 twice and became a pro, but before getting a payout I hit a −10% drawdown and lost my pro status 😢

Passing the challenge doesn't mean you can let your guard down.

Even after becoming a pro, you must always observe the drawdown limit; you aren't allowed to break the rules even once.
If your funds fall below a certain amount or percentage, pro status is stripped instantly.
It's incredibly strict.

High-leverage traders, especially those mainly using offshore accounts, are particularly ill suited to prop trading.

Many of them are casual about money management in the first place or take outrageous risks in their trading.

Specifically:

Moving stop-losses, averaging in, increasing lot size.

High-leverage traders haven't shaken those three bad habits, so a single incident can fail a prop account in the worst case.

I think it's very difficult for people who can't follow money-management rules.

The system—the rules—only lets people pass if they can use very low leverage, fix each loss properly, and build up slowly and steadily.

Conversely, I think it's very suitable for people who can do that. But honestly, if you already can, you could grow your own money without using a prop firm, lol.

So isn't it really suited to people who can follow money-management rules properly but don't have much capital to trade?

Having written all that, I'm short of funds myself, so I'm thinking of doing prop trading again.

records.translated_text:
[About Funded7]

As I understand it, Funded7 is a prop firm with quite detailed rules.

For that reason, it may be a very good fit for people who can follow the rules properly.

Withdrawal requests are possible every seven days.

However, being able to request a withdrawal does not mean it is guaranteed.

You check the rules yourself and apply when you judge that you meet the conditions.

If the review finds you don't meet the rules, withdrawal will not be permitted.

Many prop firms I've used had a system where being able to submit a withdrawal request basically meant you already met the payout conditions.

Funded7 is a little different there.

You need to understand the rules, calculate things yourself and apply responsibly.

I'll write an article covering this, Funded7's characteristics and how I felt while actually taking the challenge.

Please give me a little time 🔥

*May include affiliate links.

Honestly, I don't feel like trading my own funds anymore.
I remember the despair when I instantly lost the one million I'd worked so hard to save, trading domestic accounts and overseas FX.
Even looking at the charts while feeling nauseous, I couldn't make the slightest calm decision, lol.

The biggest change since I started using Fintokei is that “fear” has disappeared from trading.
Instead of cutting into my living expenses, I can manage tens of millions with just a small participation fee.
Ironically, that mental separation is what can make performance skyrocket.

The disqualification rules (-5% in one day, -10% overall) are certainly strict.
But they're actually the “ultimate safety net” protecting traders from ruin.
Discipline is enforced, so reckless averaging down or runaway lot sizes are physically impossible.

The immense peace of mind of knowing that losing won't damage my private life at all.
I think this is the greatest advantage—edge—for surviving today's markets.
If you're still wearing yourself out over every rise and fall in your own wallet, entering this “world of discipline” might be the shortest route to becoming a professional.

records.translated_text:
Prop firms have suddenly become very popular lately! I also used Fintokei a little while ago, passed twice, and traded as a pro trader, but in the end I was disqualified without ever making a withdrawal 🥲
Here is why I found Fintokei difficult.

① Even with unrealized losses, you're disqualified if you fall below -5% of equity.
→ It's an obvious rule, but this is the hardest part, lol.
You have to cut losses immediately. If your method is built around averaging down from the start, you can be disqualified fairly quickly unless you're careful about lot sizes.

② For that reason, pyramiding is difficult.

→ Just a small move against you can get you disqualified, lol. And if you carry unrealized profits into the next day, the -5% disqualification level is calculated from equity including those profits, making it harder. Pretty brutal.

③ Withdrawals are available every other week.
→ That was tough for me because I had debts then. I couldn't wait, lol. I'd trade while waiting and get disqualified, lol.

④ Fees are too high.
→ In addition to the spread, there's a fee when closing, and it's ridiculously expensive! Lots of scalping can leave you losing to fees, turning steady little gains into a big loss, lol.

In any case, I felt the rules were designed to our disadvantage! 🥲
I decided I'd rather trade my own money and quit.

But some people seem to withdraw successfully every time, so I think my risk management is simply poor, lol.
Anyway, it didn't fit my style.

I paid for challenge plans by credit card and spent around 800,000 (currency not stated) in total 💦

Of course, it was revolving credit, so that became debt too.
Damn it!! lol

For bad traders like me who can't even follow the 5% rule, ordinary high-leverage overseas trading has a higher expected value 💦

Ugh, people who recommend prop firms will get angry if I say things like this 🙇🙇
Sorry, I don't mean to dismiss prop firms at all.

I'm just annoyed that I spent 800,000 (currency not stated) on my credit card, lol.
I think prop trading itself offers a big chance to earn large sums from a small amount of capital, so it must be heaven for people who can follow trading rules 😆😆

Maybe they spend a lot on marketing.
If that's all a firm needs to pay annually, I'll start one at my company 🤣

Jokes aside, I think they were near the top of Kaitai's (@fxkaitaishinsho) ranking until recently, but they've dropped quite a bit now, haven't they?

You must all have been hit pretty hard by this too.
You just aren't saying so 🙄
It might be difficult unless you day trade with a swing-oriented style or hold longer.

The entry price is low and there are plenty of coupons, but it's correspondingly strict, or the exit is narrow. Like an overseas university 🤣

records.translated_text:
How to tackle Fintokei
I thought about an approach to Finokei in my own way.

① A prop firm's appeal is managing large capital with little money, but I think this creates an “illusion about the margin amount.” Since you're actually disqualified at -10%, you need to manage it as though your margin were one-tenth of the stated amount.
② Based on ①, with margin at one-tenth, Step 1 +8% becomes +80%, and Step 2 +6% becomes +60%, so it's actually quite hard.
③ FX leverage is also 100:1, but since actual capital is one-tenth, it's effectively 1,000:1.
For example, on this Crystal plan with 2 million yen in capital, trading 1.0 lot (ignoring spread and commission) at 153 yen per dollar means leverage of 7.65:1. But actual usable capital is 200,000 yen, making it 76.5:1. You end up highly leveraged even without intending to.
④ If you don't understand ③, you'll quickly hit the “maximum allowable risk for open positions of -3%” and receive a warning.

That's why prop-specific risk management is necessary. I think the only right approach is to pass slowly with leverage as low as possible.

records.translated_text:
I've decided to revise my personal rules to reduce the risk of blowing prop-firm accounts.
Combining BlueberryFunded InstantLite's maximum of seven open positions with Fintokei's 3% open-position risk rule, I'd like to reset risk per position to:

 Fintokei: 0.42% (2.94% with seven positions)
 The5ers: 0.35% (2.45% with seven positions)
 BlueberryFunded InstantLite: 0.28% (1.96% with seven positions).

For adding positions when I already hold seven,
I want to close the position I judge to have the lowest earning potential at that point and then add. Basically, I'll close the position with the lowest

 pip value × ATR × lot size

first, then add a new one. Depending on the situation, I may prioritize closing a position with an unrealized loss.

My current positions carry a bit more risk, but I intend to add while keeping within the maximum risk for seven positions stated above.

With this risk setting, I don't think I can clear Step 3 of Fintokei's introductory plan, but I'll trade steadily under my own rules to avoid blowing paid accounts.

A deadline for passing seems to encourage rushing to pass, increasing the risk of blowing an account. Such experimentation is better done in free accounts or free contests (I tell myself).

With nine months of prop-firm trading and one year nine months of FX trading, I'm still a novice, but I'll continue experimenting at my own level.

records.translated_text:
Comparing prop firms: support, from Ame-chan’s perspective

Fintokei VS Instantfunding VS fundingPips

Having used various prop firms, support is what I rely on when I have questions or encounter trouble. I would like to compare that support from my perspective.

Basically, I only compare firms I have used extensively. Please understand that I will not discuss places I have barely used or never tried.

For the best support (*´∀`)ﾉ, Fintokei wins by a landslide 🏆️

Live chat is available on the website, and email responses are fast too.

The absolute worst, needless to say, is fundingPips, the runaway winner 😠

I could confidently say that however many questions you email them, you never get a reply.

I have sent close to ten emails myself, with no replies at all.

Honestly, do they even have support staff⁉️ So I 100% cannot recommend them to anyone trying a prop firm for the first time. Better not to.

instantFunding is so-so. Their email replies are reasonably fast.

Now, for ultra-real-time support, the three rank as follows:

instantFunding・fundingPips >>>> Fintokei

What⁉️ You might think, “Isn’t Fintokei best?” But the first two actually use Discord for support or supplementary support, so if you ask there, you get a response almost within seconds.

The drawbacks are...
① Communication is basically in English.
② Difficult issues are escalated, so communication moves to email.
③ It is not one-to-one support; you ask among a group of other users.

There are plenty of questions about trading rules and payouts, so you might find what you wanted to ask beforehand (о´∀`о)

#fintokei

records.translated_text:
I was taking on Fintokei with an EA portfolio, but the EAs I run are designed to “take substantial losses when they lose, but let profits grow strongly when they catch a trend.” That makes them a poor fit for the prop-specific rule that stops trading for the day once the daily profit cap is reached.

Trading is forcibly stopped just when I want to let profits run, so I felt the portfolio’s strengths were not being fully realized.

I therefore decided to combine it with short-term discretionary trading.

My discretionary trading mainly ranges from short-term scalping to day trading. I started because I judged it would fit Fintokei’s rules well, and performance has been stable. Of the evaluation process consisting of Steps 1, 2 and 3, I am now close to clearing Step 1.

records.translated_text:
[Regarding the forced imposition of profit limits on fintokei pro accounts]

I have organized my thoughts again.

■ Introduction
Because this notice came completely out of the blue, I was deeply shocked and lost my composure. I apologize for saying many unnecessary things. Thanks to everyone, I have finally calmed down. Thank you.

■ What started this
A profit limit was imposed suddenly, without any warning.

■ Problems
① The very existence of a daily profit limit is not explicitly stated or communicated.
② The objective indicators and threshold values that trigger the daily profit limit are not explicitly stated or communicated.
③ The current approach based on total trading profit and loss can restrict gambling traders, but it also restricts traders who genuinely grew through the necessary process of learning from losing their pro status.
④ Given those three points, from the user’s perspective, the restriction is suddenly enforced without information about it or a warning.

■ Thoughts
Without ① and ②, users have no way to respond, so I think a minimum level of action is needed.

Regarding ③, if the purpose is to exclude gambling traders, the approach needs revisiting because it also excludes traders who genuinely improved while thoroughly managing their capital and not using particularly large lots. On the other hand, from the perspective of assessing a trader’s qualities, I can understand inserting a stage of trading a restricted pro account between Steps 2 and 3.

As for ④, I would appreciate a notice or warning once a trader hits fintokei’s criteria. Having the restriction imposed without warning is painful.

■ Suggestions for improvement
As I said, the fact that this came out of the blue is what started the issue.

First, please explicitly state and publicly communicate the daily profit limit. Including objective indicators and numerical thresholds would help users.

In addition to excluding gambling trading, the restrictions also affect traders who grow through experiences of disqualification. Could you either reconsider the very approach of total trading profit and loss, which does not consider the chronology of imposing restrictions, or formally include a profit-limited pro stage to better assess a trader’s professional qualities?

Also, specifying objective, concrete conditions for lifting the restriction would make it easier for us to respond, and I would greatly appreciate that.

This is not limited to this particular restriction: please send a notice or warning when we hit your criteria.

As an aside, even if you impose a restriction, isn’t a daily profit cap of 1% excessive compared with an allowable daily loss of 5%?

■ Closing
Again, I apologize for making a fuss. Because my X post gained a little traction, I learned that this is not only my personal issue; others are in similar circumstances.
They have had the same experience I did this time.
I sincerely hope we can maintain a constructive, win-win relationship.

@FintokeiJP #fintokei

Fintokei users, please leave comments if you have opinions on this matter.

If there is anything worth conveying to fintokei, I would like to do so.

For now, I have just sent the above to fintokei’s support desk.

As long as you’re fighting with “your own money,” you’ll never become a pro.

• A forced stop at a 5% daily loss.
• An objective view of it as “money entrusted to me.”

These mandatory rules are the strongest weapon for steadily building profits. Once I realized the strict rules weren’t shackles but a breakwater protecting me, my trading results quickly stabilized 😁

Ultimately, rather than endlessly tweaking methods, moving to an environment where you can systematize money management can be the shortest path to winning.

The age of draining your own money and wearing down your mental state is over.
Simply changing where you fight can completely change the view.

My thoughts on PipFarm's instant account ($20k).

First, you can't withdraw until you make 6% ($1200) profit.
The first time, you can withdraw only 50% of that ($600).
So for the first payout, rank 0 gets 70%, meaning $420.
Effectively, the reward is 35% of the profit you made.
I'm rank 4, so 90%, $560.

On top of that, you need five days with 0.25% profit,
and must maintain a 25% consistency rule.
Neither losses nor huge wins are allowed.

Conclusion: it's pretty tough lol.
The challenge is cheap, so it's an option if you can reach the finish, but it felt more like working than having fun.
Even if you buy it just for a little fun, you have to trade for at least five days.
To clear it in five days,
you need to take profits of 1.2%–1.5%.

There is profit left in the account, so making another $600 lets you withdraw again, which is a little easier. But being told to do this again from scratch might be quite tough.

Still, a $20k instant account costs $75, so maybe it's an option if you treat the share of profit you receive as half of normal?

records.translated_text:
About Funded7

Last year it was the Fintokei turmoil, and this year it’s Funded7—funny, lol.
I too had a payout of around ¥1 million refused, and I think many people have had outcomes they can’t accept 💦

Keeping those negative opinions in mind, I’d like to organize what Funded7 has done since entering Japan.

------
❶ Problems arose where people applied for payouts and were disqualified retroactively back to their evaluation accounts.
⇒ Thanks in part to the early guinea pigs, the system was revised and the issue addressed fairly quickly ⭕️

❷ Payout refusals continued under a mysterious “all-in” rule whose full details were unknown.
⇒ According to what I heard from the official team, a consistency rule was introduced to make this objective ⭕️

* But it was suddenly introduced after the fact without prior explanation ✖️
* The calculation of the profit subject to consistency is ultimately discretionary ✖️

❸ Consistency is strict.
⇒ They created a rule allowing payouts at a slightly more lenient level ⭕️
⇒ They also stated the risk violation rule explicitly so it wouldn’t be retroactive, though it seems rather complex? 🔺
(Leaving aside whether it really becomes more lenient, I think it isn’t bad for people who let profits run.)

* This time they explained it beforehand so it wouldn’t be retroactive ⭕️
------

That’s how it looks to me, and I can somewhat recognize that they’re listening to us and desperately trying to respond 😅

I can’t deny that some details feel like “No, that’s not what we meant,” but has anyone tried this hard to listen to us in the Japanese market since Fintokei?

So if they’re trying to respond, I want to see how that turns out. Of course, I really understand why everyone is angry, so I’m not trying to tell them off 💦

There was an idol of horse racing, jockey Nanako Fujita, who quit quickly after being criticized, which was a bit disappointing.

So I’m not defending them, but I hope this Nana-chan doesn’t give up, listens to the Japanese market and keeps trying.

I did want them to pay me, though 😡😡😡

records.translated_text:
Today I lost the FundedNext account I had traded for nine months and received many payouts from. The reason is very frustrating: although two trades reached TP by a tiny margin, the prop firm’s spread difference prevented TP from triggering, and they ended at SL.

The clearest lesson I take from this is that, especially at firms with high spreads, you need to consider every possibility when opening trades. Rather than setting an extremely precise TP, it makes much more sense to give up a little profit to ensure TP actually triggers.

Otherwise, trades that hit TP in your system may not hit TP in your own account. This creates serious differences between system results and your actual results. When it repeats a few times, it can lead to losing the entire account, as happened to me today.

records.translated_text:
The FAQ for Superfunded @SuperFunded_JP has been updated.

1. Keep the loss on the same trade at or below 2.5%.
Example: $1,250 or less on a 50K account.

2. Concentrating most of the balance in one or two positions and moving the SL farther away (including not setting an SL).
Example: extreme all-or-nothing trading.

3. The lot size held simultaneously exceeds twice the average lot size.
Example: endless averaging down is treated the same as martingale.

That is about it, I suppose.
I have a good impression because they spell things out instead of setting vague rules.

Make a proper scenario before entering, set SL and TP accordingly, and do not average down, and there is no problem.
Read my blog for how to build scenarios.

Morning! This is sudden, but today I started with a prop firm called The5ers!

My trading strategy requires martingale, so I would be disqualified at Fintokei.
So when I looked for a company that allows martingale, this was it lol.
I do not know if I can pass, but I will proceed carefully 💪

On the morning of 6 February 2026, I took a split position at the same time; both trades opened in the same minute. I hit stop loss.

At noon, I went long again with a split position and closed in profit.

On the last day, I took a BTCUSD position, completed the three profitable days rule, and qualified for Phase 2.
