Now I ask:

Does opening long positions five times over two different days in a pair where my bias is long make it one-sided betting?

For example, on a pair where I have a long bias (and traded according to my system), should I have opened shorts against my bias to deliberately lose money?

As you can see, things have become quite difficult in prop firms. This is my first email saying I violated a rule like this :D

records.translated_text:
A serious discussion about profit consistency

There was a time when I struggled to withdraw from Pipfarm’s consistency mode because I couldn’t meet the requirements, and I’ve kept thinking about how to tackle profit consistency.

Now Fundora has introduced a consistency rule too.
Well, from a firm’s perspective, they don’t want to recognize profits from gambling-style trades, so I understand it better than a “daily profit limit of X%” 🙃

It’s not that they won’t recognize the profit.
It’s more like, “That profit is fine, but could you reproduce it a few times?”

Quite a few firms use this, so we need to work out how to handle it.

----

That said, even if we traders aim for repeatable trades, we can’t hit home runs that often.
Even Ohtani can’t hit a home run every single time.
Statistically, there will be several outs before the next home run.
If probability leans toward outs, you can’t withdraw.

Of course, three consecutive home runs would let you withdraw, but even Hideki Matsui only did that once.
(By the way, I watched it live 😋)
------------

With that in mind, here is the management method I’m thinking about.

We traders should identify from our past results how much we make from a single hit, and set a withdrawal target at around three times that amount.
Once we make a single hit’s worth of profit, close the position for the day and continue holding that position in another account.
(Enjoy the profits from home runs or doubles in the other account.)

Set daily risk at around 0.5–0.7 times a single hit, so that a single hit the next day can recover it.
(Consistency is tough if you can’t recover.)

I think this would increase the chances of being able to withdraw quite a bit 🙄

I do not want to write at length, but this is frustrating. We know you do not want us to earn, but is there any need for this much nonsense?

You keep narrowing the room for people who put time into this work. A 1% restriction, consistency, Prime accounts, news trading. You have taken it too far.

I have enough experience and data in this industry to anticipate many things, from when a firm will offer a discount to how it will behave under certain conditions.

The prop-firm industry is changing. FundingPips, one of the leading firms, apparently is not afraid of ending up like Nokia. We struggle to keep up with rule changes coming almost every day without exception.

Previously, news-trading information came from a source shared with many other firms. For about a month, they have been including news that no other firm has in the high-impact category, making trading feel like walking through a minefield.

Every day, I note the following day's releases at the end of the day and try to structure my positions so they will not be affected. Although I checked three times that day, FundingPips listed only the meeting at 21:00 Turkish time. When I checked again at 19:00 before opening a position, there was still just one release.

By the end of the day, my profit was erased on the grounds of high-impact news conjured up from various places.

I am not even asking how you expect us to manage positions within a 1% restriction when they close $10 below my stop. With the 1% restriction presented as good news when going live, closing $10 below the stop two or three times a month wipes out accounts.

I knew this would happen when it was first introduced. Pips has made its final move. Even if behind-the-scenes activity extends its life, it will now enter stagnation and decline and lose market share.

I was not wrong about Alpha before. Nor about The5ers. I do not think I will be wrong about Pips either.

My password should be correct… Just in case, I tried resetting it.

Huh? That gives an error too. It says to try again later… Maybe a temporary problem?

Recommended for people who are not yet earning from FX or whose results are inconsistent 🙆‍♀️

I regularly take Fintokei prop challenges to maintain my trading style.

People may imagine prop firms have strict rules, but I think Fintokei only has rules that are essential to surviving in FX and growing your money. I mean Fintokei, though 💦. I do not know about the others 🤷.

The most important thing in FX is overwhelmingly money management, not which trading method you use 👩🏻‍🏫. Even someone excellent at entries needs this skill.

After many years in the markets, you learn more entry techniques and spot more opportunities, so you also have more chances to enter 🙆‍♀️🙆‍♀️. But no matter how good the method, you cannot retain money without money management 😭.

That is why I regularly take Fintokei challenges: to establish the basis of my money management and keep my lot sizing and SL/TP placement consistent. If you can do that, the prop evaluation is not particularly difficult. Conversely, it feels very difficult when your money management is poor.

I have passed several times in the past 💮, made withdrawals and enjoyed the rewards 🤤💃💃💃.

I think evaluations and the professional accounts after passing are very useful for learning and refining money management.

If you are searching X for other people's advance trade calls or trying to imitate skilled traders, first try a prop evaluation—even the cheapest account is fine. I think you will discover that the knowledge you lack is not an entry method.

Since I began using prop firms, I feel my trading style has become more stable 🙋‍♀️.

Honestly, instead of endlessly searching for entry methods, buying pullbacks and selling rallies based on Dow Theory, with SL/TP in appropriate places, should grow your money 💰.

What matters is how much of the money in your account you can afford to lose. Think first about how much you may lose; winning and the amount come afterwards 🙆‍♀️.

I think you can learn efficiently while earning.
#フィントケイ #FINTOKEI

My first instant-funded account, and my first dollar-denominated account.

Day two with TradeifyFX, a prop firm whose name I still do not even know how to pronounce.

After stopping out of a long and reversing short, I finished up $15.

Price turned just short of my take-profit target of 4107.12, and I was considering exiting. Then my closest friend, who went to Goku with me today, called.

I spoke on behalf of their mother, who has dementia, listened to both sides, calmed them down and gave a brief explanation of dementia before ending the call.

During the call, price rose 50 pips and my unrealized profit shrank to about two-thirds (˙ཫ˙). Is this the downside of phone trading?

Total result: +$141.10, a little over ¥22,000.

For now, what I think about TradeifyFX is that execution is excellent. So far, no slippage at all. Exact fills.

I have become used to Fintokei, where even limit orders sometimes slip around 10 pips, so this is surprising and delightful.

The spread feels a little wide at 3.5 pips, but if fills stay this precise, it is not bad 🥸. In fact, the trading environment is excellent.

If withdrawals are smooth too, I will have nothing to complain about 💰. No matter how good the environment, it means nothing if you cannot make profits and withdraw them 🙃.

To put it mildly, Fintokei's response was amazing. Because they processed it immediately, the money arrived the same day. My domestic bank was also fantastic. Atsuro, thank you for telling me a domestic account was fine 😊.

Without this payment, I really would have ended up 'like Kurumi-chan's mother.'
